arxiv-2107-08585.title: Rethinking binary hyperparameters for deep transfer learning for image classification
arxiv-2107-08585.creator: Jo Plested, Xuyang Shen, Tom Gedeon
arxiv-2107-08585.description: Abstract The current standard for a variety of computer vision tasks using smaller numbers of labelled training examples is to fine-tune from weights pre-trained on a large image classification dataset such as ImageNet. The application of transfer learning and transfer learning methods tends to be rigidly binary. A model is either pre-trained or not pre-trained.

arxiv-2108-08960.title: Plug and Play, Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2108-08960.creator: Majid Abdolshah, Hung Le, Thommen Karimpanal George, Sunil Gupta, Santu Rana, Svetha Venkatesh
arxiv-2108-08960.description: Abstract Sample-efficient generalisation of reinforcement learning approaches have always been a challenge, especially, for complex scenes with many components. In this work, we introduce Plug and Play Markov Decision Processes, an object-based representation that allows zero-shot integration of new objects from known object classes.

arxiv-2203-17245.title: Random cubic planar graphs converge to the Brownian sphere
arxiv-2203-17245.creator: Marie Albenque, Éric Fusy, Thomas Lehéricy
arxiv-2203-17245.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marie Albenque, Éric Fusy, Thomas Lehéricy. In this paper, the scaling limit of random connected cubic planar graphs (respectively multigraphs) is shown to be the Brownian sphere. The proof consists in essentially two main steps. First, thanks to the known decomposition of cubic planar graphs into their 3-connected components, the metric structure of a random cubic planar graph is shown to be well approximated by its unique 3-connected component of linear size, with modified distances.

arxiv-2207-02588.creator: L. Bertini, D. Gabrielli, C. Landim
arxiv-2207-02588.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by L. Bertini, D. Gabrielli, C. Landim. We examine two analytical characterisation of the metastable behavior of a Markov chain. The first one expressed in terms of its transition probabilities, and the second one in terms of its large deviations rate functional. Consider a sequence of continuous-time Markov chains ( X t ( n ) : t ≥ 0 ) (X^{(n)}_{t}:t\geq 0) evolving on a fixed finite state space V V .

arxiv-2309-10603.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Giulia Ciacci Andrea Barucci Sara Di Ruzza, Elisa Maria Alessi. We consider four different kinds of motion in mean motion resonance with the planet, nominally Tadpole , Horseshoe and Quasi-satellite , building 3 datasets defined as Real (taking the ephemerides of real asteroids from the JPL Horizons system), Ideal and Perturbed (both simulated, obtained by propagating initial conditions considering two different dynamical systems) for training

arxiv-2501-07599.title: Analyzing Spatio-Temporal Dynamics of Dissolved Oxygen for the River Thames using Superstatistical Methods and Machine Learning
arxiv-2501-07599.creator: Hankun He 1 ∗ \,{}^{1*} , Takuya Boehringer 2 \,{}^{2} , Benjamin Schäfer 3 \,{}^{3} , Kate Heppell 4 , 5 \,{}^{4,5} , Christian Beck
arxiv-2501-07599.description: Abstract By employing superstatistical methods and machine learning, we analyze time series data of water quality indicators for the River Thames (UK). The indicators analyzed include dissolved oxygen, temperature, electrical conductivity, pH, ammonium, turbidity, and rainfall, with a specific focus on the dynamics of dissolved oxygen.

arxiv-2505-02369.title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization with Z-Score Gradient Filtering
arxiv-2505-02369.creator: Vincent-Daniel Yun
arxiv-2505-02369.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vincent-Daniel Yun. Deep neural networks achieve high performance across many domains but can still face challenges in generalization when optimization is influenced by small or noisy gradient components. Sharpness-Aware Minimization improves generalization by perturbing parameters toward directions of high curvature, but it uses the entire gradient vector, which means that small or noisy components may affect the ascent step and cause the optimizer to miss optimal solutions. We propose Z-Score Filtered Sharpness-Aware Minimization, which applies Z-score based filtering to gradients in each layer.

arxiv-2509-05962.title: The Reel Deal: Designing and Evaluating LLM-Generated Short-Form Educational Videos Conference: CHIGreece 2025: 3rd International Conference of the ACM Greek SIGCHI Chapter; September 24–26, 2025; Hermoupolis, Syros, Greece CHIGreece 2025: 3rd International Conference of the ACM Greek SIGCHI Chapter

arxiv-2509-05962.description: Abstract . Short-form videos are gaining popularity in education due to their concise and accessible format that enables microlearning. Yet, most of these videos are manually created. Even for those automatically generated using artificial intelligence (AI), it is not well understood whether or how they affect learning outcomes, user experience, and trust.

arxiv-2602-08187.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Cindy Peng, Megan Chai, Gao Mo, Naveen Raman, Ningjing Tang, Shannon Pagdon, Margaret Swarbrick, Nev Jones, Fei Fang, Hong Shen. Peer-run organizations (PROs) provide critical, recovery-based behavioral health support rooted in lived experience. As large language models (LLMs) enter this domain, their scale, conversationality, and opacity introduce new challenges for situatedness, trust, and autonomy.

pmc-10577230.title: A novel Pinellia ternata catalase gene PtCAT2 regulates drought tolerance in Arabidopsis by modulating ROS balance
pmc-10577230.creator: Juanjuan Xu, Ni Du, Tianci Dong, Han Zhang, Tao Xue, Fei Zhao, Fenglan Zhao, Yongbo Duan, Jianping Xue
pmc-10577230.description: Drought is one of the major abiotic stresses limiting agricultural production, particularly for shallow-rooted plants like Pinellia ternata. It damages plants via oxidative burst, but this effect could be mitigated by catalase (CAT). However, no studies have been reported on CAT homologs in P. ternata, a drought-sensitive plant species.

pmc-11408120.title: A rare case of tracheal squamous cell carcinoma presented with critical airway obstruction
pmc-11408120.creator: Chen‐Yu Ho, Yu‐Wei Liu, Wei‐An Lai, Chia‐Min Chen, Kuan‐Li Wu
pmc-11408120.description: Key messageTracheal squamous cell carcinoma is a rare and potentially fatal thoracic cancer mimicking common airway disorders. Accurate diagnosis requires a detailed history, thorough physical examination, and high clinical suspicion. CLINICAL IMAGE A 77‐year‐old female presented with progressive shortness of breath, persistent cough, wheezing, and exertional dyspnea for 1 month.

pmc-11414554.title: A rare pediatric case of FDG-avid synovial herniation pits
pmc-11414554.creator: Karan Bir Singh, Monica A. Rossleigh, Sumanth Nagabushan, Ivan Ho Shon
pmc-11414554.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Synovial herniation pits are benign, round radiolucent lesions surrounded by a thin sclerotic rim within the superolateral aspect of the proximal femoral neck that are most commonly seen in the physically active adult population. Here we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first pediatric case of synovial herniation pits showing focal FDG uptake on a PET/CT scan in a 15 year old boy with Hodgkin's Lymphoma.

pmc-11480379.title: An automatic tracking method to measure the mandibula movement during real time MRI
pmc-11480379.creator: Jérémy Mouchoux, Florian Sojka, Philipp Kauffmann, Peter Dechent, Philipp Meyer-Marcotty, Anja Quast
pmc-11480379.description: Mandibular movement is complex and individual due to variations in the temporomandibular joint (TMJ). Consequently, patient-centered dentistry should incorporate patients’ specific anatomy and condylar function in treatment planning. Real-time magnetic resonance imaging (rt-MRI) visualizes relevant structures and tracks mandibular movement. However, current assessments rely on qualitative observations or time-consuming manual tracking, lacking reliability.

pmc-11862256.title: Piled-up Risk Factors: a Case Report of Diogenes Syndrome
pmc-11862256.creator: J. L. Freixo, S. G. Rodrigues, T. Novo, D. Brandão
pmc-11862256.description: IntroductionDiogenes Syndrome (DS) is an uncommon neurobehavioral syndrome characterized by social isolation, extreme neglect of personal care and a tendency to excessively accumulate useless objects in the home, usually leading to unsanitary living conditions. It is further characterized by a lack of insight into the condition, leading to a refusal to seek assistance.

pmc-11879511.title: Subjective Successful Aging in the Presence of Mobility Disability
pmc-11879511.creator: Madina Khamzina, Wendy A Rogers, Nicholas G Castle
pmc-11879511.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and ObjectivesResearchers often define successful aging as freedom from disability and disease, yet the perceptions of older adults living with disability challenge this conception, demonstrating that they can indeed age successfully.

pmc-12640482.title: Antecedents of data analytics adoption: A systematic literature review from 2018-2024
pmc-12640482.creator: Alqa Husni, Wasanthi Madurapperuma, Ranpati Dewage Thilini Sumudu Kumari, Tarun Kumar Vashishth, Alexandra Theodoropoulou, Alexandra Theodoropoulou, Alqa Husni, Tarun Kumar Vashishth, Alqa Husni
pmc-12640482.description: BackgroundThe rise of data analytics adoption has transformed multiple industries through technological advancements. However, utilizing big data analytics presents challenges that depend on adoption models used by individuals or organizations. Whilst numerous models on big data analytics exist, understanding the most influential theories shaping research in this domain remains limited.

pmc-13077807.title: Could non-humans have Traditional Ecological Knowledge? And if so, what should we do about it?
pmc-13077807.creator: Elodie Freymann, Fabien Schultz, Daniel Redfearn
pmc-13077807.description: Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) has historically been understood as uniquely human. However, emerging evidence from elephants, cetaceans, chimpanzees and other intelligent species suggests that some animal communities maintain and transmit ecological knowledge across generations in ways comparable to human TEK.

pmc-13186149.title: Predictors of Mortality and Outcomes in Older Adult Burn Patient Subgroups: A Comparative Meta-analysis of Age, Burn Severity, and Intervention Strategies
pmc-13186149.creator: Yomna E. Dean, Mohamed I. Mohamed, Alaa Alqadi, Abu Omayer, Dina Elsayed, Abdulrahman Shokri, Rashed W. Alweshah, Shree Rath, Israa Alam, Moussa Nassar, Kevin McGarry
pmc-13186149.description: Background:Older adult burn patients experience disproportionately high morbidity and mortality due to age-related physiological decline and comorbidities. Understanding predictors of mortality is essential for risk stratification and improving outcomes. This meta-analysis evaluates mortality predictors and clinical outcomes among older adult burn patients, stratified into a younger cohort (60-79 y) and an older cohort (80+ y).

pmc-13273575.title: Simultaneous saddle pulmonary embolism and right atrial thrombus managed with ICE-guided dual suction Thrombectomy
pmc-13273575.creator: Ibraheem Sabah, Sakeena Saife, Ahmad Nouri, Tamim Khaddash, Sarah Bhanushali, Ibrahim Khaddash, Fayez Shamoon
pmc-13273575.description: Saddle pulmonary embolism (PE) complicated by right atrial thrombus in transit is an infrequent but highly lethal condition. Standard treatments such as systemic thrombolysis or surgical embolectomy carry significant risks, particularly in elderly or comorbid patients. We describe the case of a 76-year-old man with spina bifida, cauda equina syndrome, chronic immobility, and multiple comorbidities who presented in shock.

pmc-13472075.title: Proceedings of the Global Health Focus Youth Conference 2025: The Role of Young People in Advancing Global Health Education, Research, and Leadership
pmc-13472075.creator: Zhinya Kawa Othman, Don Eliseo Lucero‐Prisno, Mohamed Mustaf Ahmed, Olalekan John Okesanya, Aniekan Michael Ekpenyong, Jerico Bautista Ogaya, Goodness Ogeyi Odey, Adriana Viola Miranda, Yasir Ahmed Mohammed Elhadi, Yusuff Adebayo Adebisi
pmc-13472075.description: Youth represent the largest and most interconnected generation but remain underserved by traditional and global health structures. In Africa alone, nearly 60% of the population is under the age of 25, and the continent's youthful population is projected to reach almost 1 billion by 2050.

pmc-13635506.title: Segmented poly(A) tails with microRNA target sites confer tissue-specific regulation for mRNA therapeutics
pmc-13635506.creator: Rui Qi, Hua Chen, Rui Chen, Hui Bao, Ying Sun, Ruiwen Xu, Lu Han, Yingmei Xu, Juan Li, Na Li, Qiang Li, Tingting Zhang, Kai Lv, Yijie Dong, Shan Cen, Weiguo Zhang
pmc-13635506.description: Targeted delivery and controlled expression of mRNA encapsulated by lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) are critical for the development of safe and effective mRNA medicines. However, efficient post-delivery regulation of mRNA-LNP expression remains challenging, and conventional approaches largely rely on modifying the 3′ UTR at the expense of other regulatory elements.

pmc-13689365.title: Bacterial R-bodies with common morphologies and unrolling dynamics are phylogenetically scattered, indicating extensive lateral gene transfer and wide application potential
pmc-13689365.creator: Lennart Dörr, Robin Ghosh, Michael Schweikert
pmc-13689365.description: Refractile bodies (R-bodies) of gram-negative bacteria are large proteinaceous assemblies, rolled up in the form of an Archimedean spiral. They exhibit rapid rod-like reversible extension in the micrometer range when cued by chemical environmental triggers and have potential for synthetic biology and biochip applications.
